question: What orientation and locator-tone requirements apply to an accessible pedestrian push button?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Each accessible pedestrian push button must have a vibrotactile arrow on the button itself, with high visual contrast, aligned parallel to the direction of travel on the associated crosswalk, so pedestrians with vision disabilities can identify which crossing it actuates and align themselves. A locator tone is also mandatory to help pedestrians locate the vibrotactile arrow and the push button; the tone may be deactivated during the steady DONT WALK display only if passive pedestrian detection reactivates it whenever a pedestrian is within 12 feet. Standards (mandatory): - "Each push button shall clearly indicate by means of a vibrotactile arrow which crosswalk signal is actuated by the push button. Vibrotactile arrows shall be located on the button of the push button assembly, shall have high visual contrast (light on dark or dark on light), and shall be aligned parallel to the direction of travel on the associated crosswalk." - "A locator tone shall be incorporated into the accessible pedestrian signal equipment to help pedestrians with vision disabilities locate the vibrotactile arrow, and the associated push button if a push button is provided." Guidance (recommended): - In temporary traffic control contexts, if a pushbutton is used to provide equivalent TTC information to pedestrians with vision disabilities, it should be equipped with a locator tone to notify pedestrians that a special accommodation is available and to help them locate the pushbutton. Options (permitted): - The locator tone may default to a deactivated mode while the steady UPRAISED HAND (DONT WALK) indication is displayed, provided a passive pedestrian detection system activates the tone whenever a pedestrian is present within a 12-foot radius of the push button (except when the audible walk indication is active); where pedestrian facilities such as sidewalks are present, the passive detection requirement may be reduced to apply only to pedestrians on those facilities within the 12-foot radius. Citations: - Section 4K.04 Standard §1 (p.734) - Section 4K.04 Standard §2 (p.734) - Section 6C.03 Guidance §8 (p.781) - Section 4K.04 Option §5 (p.734) - Section 4K.04 Support §3 (p.734) - Section 4K.01 Support §11 (p.731)
gold_answer: The push button must have a high-contrast vibrotactile arrow on the button, aligned parallel to travel on the associated crosswalk. A locator tone must be incorporated; normally it is 0.15 seconds or less and repeats at 1-second intervals when the audible walk indication is not active, subject to stated exceptions.
